outputs.exact_statement:
There is a universal constant $C_{\mathrm{ap}}>0$ such that for every $0<\varepsilon<1$ there is an integer $R(\varepsilon)\leq C_{\mathrm{ap}}\varepsilon^{-6}$ with the following property. Let $M\subseteq\mathcal B(H)$ be a complex von Neumann algebra, let $A\subseteq M$ be a MASA, and let $x=x^*\in M$. For every finite $F\subset H$ and every $\delta>0$, there exist $y=y^*\in M$, a partition $\mathcal P=(p_i)_{i=1}^{R(\varepsilon)}$ of the unit in $A$, and $a=a^*\in A$, such that $$\left\lVert y\right\rVert\leq3\left\lVert x\right\rVert,\qquad
 \left\lVert(y-x)\xi\right\rVert<\delta\quad(\xi\in F),$$ and $$\left\lVert a\right\rVert\leq\left\lVert y\right\rVert,\qquad
 \left\lVert C_{\mathcal P}(y)-a\right\rVert\leq\varepsilon\left\lVert y\right\rVert.$$ Zero projections may be included in the partition.

Suppose that a MASA $A\subseteq M$ is the range of a normal conditional expectation. For each $0<\varepsilon<1$ there is an integer $R_s(\varepsilon)$, independent of the inclusion, such that for every $x=x^*\in M$ and every strong-operator neighborhood $\mathcal V$ of zero, there exist an $R_s(\varepsilon)$-partition $\mathcal P$ in $A$, an $a=a^*\in A$ with $\left\lVert a\right\rVert\leq\left\lVert x\right\rVert$, and a projection $q\in M$ with $\mathbf 1-q\in\mathcal V$, satisfying $$\left\lVert q(C_{\mathcal P}(x)-a)q\right\rVert\leq\varepsilon\left\lVert x\right\rVert.$$

There is a universal constant $C>0$ such that for every $0<\varepsilon<1$ one can choose an integer $N(\varepsilon)\leq C\varepsilon^{-2}$ with the following property. If the MASA $A\subseteq M$ is the range of a normal conditional expectation, then the conclusion of Theorem 1 holds with $N(\varepsilon)$ in place of $R(\varepsilon)$.

Every $A$-partition compression $C_{\mathcal Q}$ preserves $\varphi$ and is contractive for both state seminorms. As $\mathcal Q$ refines through all finite $A$-partitions, $$C_{\mathcal Q}(z)\longrightarrow E_A(z)
 \quad\text{in }\left\lVert\cdot\right\rVert_\varphi^\#
 \qquad(z\in M).$$ The same holds along any refining sequence of partitions generating $A$.

Let $$\mathcal I_\varphi=
 \{(z_j)\in\ell^\infty(M):\left\lVert z_j\right\rVert_\varphi^\#\to0\},$$ and let $$\mathcal C_\varphi=
 \{t\in\ell^\infty(M):
 t\mathcal I_\varphi\subseteq\mathcal I_\varphi,\
 \mathcal I_\varphi t\subseteq\mathcal I_\varphi\}.$$ Then $\mathcal C_\varphi$ is a unital $C^*$-algebra and $\mathcal I_\varphi$ is a closed two-sided ideal in it. Constant sequences from $M$ and all sequences in $\ell^\infty(A)$ belong to $\mathcal C_\varphi$.

Put $t_i^{1/2}=\mathop{\mathrm{diag}}(\sqrt{t_{vi}})_{v\in Q}$. Then $$\label{poly:differential-formula} f_Q(Y)= \left(\prod_{v\in Q}\frac{1}{r!}\partial_{Y_v}^{r-1}\right) \prod_{i=1}^r \det\bigl(\mathop{\mathrm{diag}}(Y+a)-r t_i^{1/2}Wt_i^{1/2}\bigr).$$ This identity remains valid for complex $t_{vi}$ with $\sum_i t_{vi}=1$, where the expectation means the finite algebraic sum with the corresponding product weights, and the same square root is used in both occurrences of $t_i^{1/2}$. The algebraic identity also holds with complex penalties and arbitrary complex off-diagonal entries of $W$, still with zero diagonal.* *More generally, let $\mathcal H$ be an open half-plane. If the product of determinants on the right of [poly:differential-formula], for every principal restriction, is nonzero whenever all its variables lie in $\mathcal H$, then the same holds for $f_Q$. In particular, for Hermitian $W$ and real probabilities and penalties, $f_Q$ is upper-half-plane stable and its univariate specialization is real-rooted.

Let $T$ be a Hermitian contraction on a nonempty finite index set $Q$, with zero diagonal. In [poly:definition], take $W=T$, $a_v=0$, and $t_{vi}=1/r$. Then $$\label{poly:mss-bound} \max\operatorname{root}(f_Q)\leq2\sqrt{2/r}+2/r.$$ In particular, giving every vertex the same penalty $b$ places all roots strictly below zero if $2\sqrt{2/r}+2/r

Suppose $a=1$ in [poly:general-arrow], and set $H=\int|x|\,d\gamma(x)=1+2m$. There is a universal $C_0$ such that $$\begin{aligned} \sum_{|s_j|\leq60H}\nu_j&\leq C_0H^2, \label{poly:near-mass}\\ \sum_{s_j\geq20H}\frac{\nu_j}{s_j}&\leq C_0m, \label{poly:positive-tail}\\ \sum_{s_j\leq-20H}\frac{\nu_j}{|s_j|}&\leq C_0H. \label{poly:negative-tail} \end{aligned}$$ For example, $C_0=6000$ suffices.

For finitely many real poles $s_j$, nonnegative weights $w_j$, and $c>0$, $$\label{poly:boole-identities}
 \left|\left\{\lambda\in\mathbb R:
       \sum_j\frac{w_j}{\lambda-s_j}>c\right\}\right|
 =\left|\left\{\lambda\in\mathbb R:
       \sum_j\frac{w_j}{\lambda-s_j}<-c\right\}\right|
 =\frac{\sum_jw_j}{c}.$$ If every pole carrying positive weight is strictly positive, the first exceedance set lies in $(0,\infty)$.

There are universal constants $K\geq1$ and $C>0$ with the following property. In [poly:general-arrow], let a finite family of choices have masses $ u_{ij}\geq0$ and probabilities $t_i\geq0$ such that $\sum_i t_i=1$ and $\sum_i t_i u_{ij}= u_j$. Keep the poles $s_j$ unchanged, and define $$h_i'(z)=z+Ka-\sum_j rac{ u_{ij}}{z-s_j}, \qquad \ell_i'=L(Ka, u_i),\qquad \ell=L(a, u).$$ Then $$\label{poly:buffered-pin-bound} \min_{i:t_i>0}\ell_i'\leq\ell+Cm.$$ The constants have no dependence on the number or positions of the poles, the masses, the probabilities, or the positive penalty $a$.

There is a universal constant $K\geq1$ with the following property. Suppose $T$, $\mathcal R$, $\mathcal G$, and $\omega$ satisfy the preceding assumptions. Let $b>0$, and choose a positive integer $r$ such that $$2\sqrt{2/r}+2/r<b.
 \label{slab:r-choice}$$ For every $\sigma>0$ and $\rho>0$, there is a measurable coloring of $V$ with $r+1$ colors for which $$\int_V \bigl((T_{\mathrm{pav}}-(Kb+\sigma)\mathbf 1)_+^2\bigr)_{vv}
 \,d\mu(v)<\rho.
 \label{slab:measured-conclusion}$$

On each bounded slab, the finite local functions $h_u,G_u,h_{u,i},h_{u,i}',R_{u,i}$, the probability and residue measures, and the data $m_u,\ell_u,\ell_{u,i}'$ have unique limits as finite graph balls increase to a component. They are measurable and independent of the exhaustion, and the local Cauchy-transform and Poisson-transform identities pass to the limits. Their supports have a common fixed-slab bound, and Equation [slab:local-bounds] continues to hold.* *The Laurent coefficients through order $k$ of $h_u/z$, $zG_u$, $h_{u,i}/z$, $h_{u,i}'/z$, and $R_{u,i}$, and the moments of $\gamma_u$ through order $k$, depend only on the data within graph distance $k$ of $u$. The same assertion holds for coefficients of logarithmic derivatives under data perturbations, with the local perturbation directions included in the data. It remains valid under arbitrary deletion configurations.* *At an unassigned vertex the buffered pin inequality of Lemma 11 holds for these infinite local data. If every base vertex is unassigned, then $m_u=0$ on every bounded slab.

Consider any bounded slab containing $V\times[0,1]$, any base partial assignment, and any further measurable restriction that retains the central vertices being tested. Deleting a measurable set of vertices at heights $s>R$, or at heights $s<-R$, changes the tuple in Equation [slab:normalized-data] by an amount tending to zero in $L^1(d\mu\,ds)$ on the central unassigned band as $R\to\infty$. The convergence is uniform in the slab, the partial assignment, and the deletion set. The same conclusion holds for the union of a far high set and a far low set.

For every $\tau_0>0$ there are arbitrarily large integers $L\geq1$ with the following property, uniformly over all base partial assignments. On the slab $V\times[0,L]$ one can choose a measurable prospective color $i(v)$ at each unassigned base vertex, using the same color at every height, so that $$\frac1L\int_{\mathrm{unassigned}\ \mathrm{in}\ V\times[0,L]} (\ell_{(v,s),i(v)}'-\ell_{(v,s)})\,d\widetilde\mu(v,s) \leq C\Phi+\tau_0, \qquad \Phi=\frac1L\int_{V\times[0,L]}m_{(v,s)}\,d\widetilde\mu(v,s). \label{slab:coherent-inequality}$$ Here $C$ is the universal constant in Lemma 11, and every $\ell_{u,i}'$ on the left is the insertion cost after changing only the lifted vertex $u$. The same $L$ can be used at every stage of a sequence of partial assignments.

For every $\gamma>0$ there is an integer $R_{\mathrm{st}}(\gamma)$ with the following property. For every self-adjoint $x\in M$ with $\left\lVert x\right\rVert\leq1$, there are partitions $\mathcal P_j$ of $1$ in $A$, each with $R_{\mathrm{st}}(\gamma)$ members, and self-adjoint $w_j\in M$ such that $$\label{exp:state-paving}
 \left\lVert w_j\right\rVert\leq2,\qquad
 \left\lVert w_j\right\rVert_\varphi\longrightarrow0,\qquad
 \left\lVert C_{\mathcal P_j}(x-w_j)-E_A(x)\right\rVert\leq\gamma.$$ The integer $R_{\mathrm{st}}(\gamma)$ is independent of $M,A,\varphi$, and $x$.
Let $b,\sigma>0$ and let $r$ be an integer such that $$2\sqrt{2/r}+2/r12.

For every $n\geq2$, there are sequences of $n$-partitions in $A$ whose quotient partition $\mathcal P$ satisfies $$\label{exp:off-normalizer-bound}
 \left\lVert C_{\mathcal P}[Z]\right\rVert\leq\frac4{\sqrt n}.$$
If $E_N(X)=0$, then $k_X(v,\cdot)$ has no atoms for almost every $v\in V$.

Let $\mathcal M$ have separable predual, let $\phi_0$ be a faithful normal state, and let $D\subset\mathcal M_{\phi_0}$ be a diffuse MASA. Suppose that $U\in\mathcal M$ is a self-adjoint unitary with $\phi_0(U)=0$, and that the normal positive map $$\mathcal K(a)=E_D(UaU),\qquad a\in D,$$ has an almost everywhere diffuse kernel on a standard probability model of $(D,\phi_0|_D)$. For every integer $n\geq2$ there are unitaries $w_l\in D$, with $w_l^n=1$, such that the joint star moments of $(w_l,U)$ converge to those of free unitaries $(w,U_{\mathrm f})$, where $w$ is uniform on the $n$th roots of unity and $U_{\mathrm f}$ is uniform on $\{-1,1\}$.

Let $w$ and $U_{\mathrm f}$ have the free law in Lemma 22, in its reduced free-product representation. If $p_1,\ldots,p_n$ are the spectral projections of $w$, then $$\label{exp:free-norm-bound} \left\lVert\sum_{j=1}^n p_j U_{\mathrm f}p_j\right\rVert\leq\frac2{\sqrt n}.$$
The conclusion of Theorem 18 holds without the assumption of separable predual, with the same partition-size bound.

Under the hypotheses of Lemma 25, let $P$ act normally on a Hilbert space and let $x=x^*\in P$ satisfy $\left\lVert x\right\rVert\leq1$. For each $m\geq2$, the operators $sxs$ supplied by that lemma approximate $x$ strongly, with associated $m$-partitions $\mathcal P$ satisfying $$\left\lVert sxs\right\rVert\leq1,\qquad \left\lVert C_{\mathcal P}(sxs)\right\rVert\leq1/m.$$ Here the approximation is on any prescribed finite set of vectors, to any positive accuracy, while $m$ stays fixed.

For any MASA $A\subset M$, set $$e=\bigvee\{\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}(\lambda):\lambda\in M_*^+,
                  \ \lambda\text{ centralizes }A\},\qquad h=\mathbf 1-e.$$ Then $e,h\in A$. If $e\ne0$, there is a faithful normal conditional expectation $E:eMe\to Ae$. If $h\ne0$, the inclusion $Ah\subset hMh$ has no nonzero centralizing normal positive functional.
